c1: On p. 17 the article says no pedestals were found in the entire sounding on the southern island. I have dug briquetage sites on this coast: their waste heaps are always full of pedestal fragments, because the jars stood on pedestals over the fire. A deposit of jar sherds with no pedestals at all is not a salt workshop. So SU 104 is more likely a dump of broken storage jars, and the southern island should not be read as a briquetage site.
c2: What did we say about Caprolace?
That's wrong: my position is that the southern island is still undecided, not that SU 104 is a dump of storage jars.
